title: Pressure
seo_title: Year 9 Science: Pressure Worksheets (Pressure = Force ÷ Area, Liquids, Upthrust)
standard_text: Atmospheric pressure, decreases with increase of height as weight of air above decreases with height; pressure in liquids, increasing with depth; upthrust effects, floating and sinking; pressure measured by ratio of force over area – acting normal to any surface.
meta_desc: Free Year 9 science worksheets on pressure: pressure = force ÷ area, everyday examples, pressure in liquids and gases, atmospheric pressure, upthrust and floating. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Smaller area means bigger pressure; liquid pressure rises with depth.
body_html:
How to think about it

Pressure is how concentrated a force is.

  • pressure = force ÷ area (N/m² or Pa). Small area → big pressure; big area → small pressure.
  • Pressure in a liquid increases with depth. Air pressure decreases with height.
  • Upthrust is the upward push of a liquid or gas: an object floats when upthrust equals its weight.
Example

600 N on 2 m²?

600 ÷ 2

Answer: 300 N/m²

Example

Snowshoes: pressure up or down?

Bigger area

Answer: down

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a bigger area gives a bigger pressure.
  • Thinking pressure is the same as force.
  • Thinking air pressure increases as you climb.

faq.a: Divide the force by the area: pressure = force ÷ area. With force in newtons and area in m², the answer is in N/m² (pascals).

faq.q: Why does pressure increase with depth in water?
faq.a: The deeper you go, the more water there is above you, and its weight pushes down harder.
The water pushes up with a force called upthrust. If the upthrust can balance the object's weight, it floats.

items.q: A force of 2,500 N gives a pressure of 500 N/m². What is the area?
A force of 200 N gives a pressure of 200 N/m². What is the area?
Why does a drawing pin have a sharp point and a wide head?
c: Both ends give the same pressure.
The point gives a high pressure on the board; the head gives a low pressure on your thumb.
items.e: Same force: smaller area → bigger pressure; bigger area → smaller pressure.

A crate pushes down with a force of 400 N on an area of 2 m². What pressure does it exert?
Why do high heels damage some floors more than flat shoes?
c: Pressure does not depend on area.
Flat shoes have a smaller area.
The small heel area gives a much larger pressure.
items.e: Same force: smaller area → bigger pressure; bigger area → smaller pressure.

items.q: What is the unit of pressure?
c: newtons per square metre (N/m²), also called pascals (Pa)

items.q: Why do snowshoes stop you sinking into snow?

items.q: What causes the pressure of a gas in a container?
c: Particles colliding with the walls of the container

What is pressure?
c: the force acting on each unit of area
